newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Chernomorneftegaz eyes new Shell venture.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Chernomorneftegaz eyes new Shell venture.

text.p: Ukraine's Chernomorneftegaz energy company plans to set up a joint venture with Royal Dutch/Shell Group by 1997 to explore oil reserves on the Black Sea shelf, Ukraine's Oil and Gas Bulletin said on Friday.
The weekly independent bulletin quoted Chernomorneftegaz Deputy President Fyodor Uryupin as saying the two sides had reached an agreement in recent talks.
"The agreement should be signed by Chernomorneftegaz and Shell by the end of the year," Uryupin was qouted as saying.
The bulletin also said Chernomorneftegaz President Nikolai Ilnitsky had announced the withdrawal of his company from a 55-45 joint venture with British JKX Oil and Gas Plc.
Shell has already secured four drilling licences for Ukrainian reserves and Kiev said recently it would look favourably on Shell's proposal to drill for offshore oil.
Ukrainian officials said in July that Shell unit Shell Pecten was considering investing up to $1 billion in natural gas pipeline and oil drilling projects in the former Soviet republic.
Ukraine recently granted tax relief to foreign oil exploration companies, linking the breaks to the efficiency of equipment used in Ukrainian energy projects.
